subject: Post-call: Multilang qualification checklist + prompt sets (EU & APAC)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Anna Schubert <anna.schubert@linguaworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: Multilang qualification checklist + prompt sets (EU & APAC)

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a concrete checklist so we can qualify model fit for LinguaWorks' international chat assistant: 

Summary of needs (from call)
- Target languages: German (de), French (fr), European Spanish (es-ES) — primary EU set.
- APAC priority: Japanese (ja) and Korean (ko) for later phase.
- Latency target: 95th <= 350ms for single-turn small responses (100–150 tokens).
- Throughput: bursty peaks ~120 concurrent sessions.
- Data residency: EU-only for EU users; will require VPC/private deployment or dedicated routing.
- Quality sensitivity: idiomatic correctness and style preservation > raw BLEU. Hallucination tolerance is low for product-critical answers.

Immediate qualification checklist (what we need from LinguaWorks)
1) Small labeled dev/test sets per locale (sample: 200–500 pairs, incl. idioms) — Anna to share a sample dataset by EOD next Tue (2026-11-24).
2) Representative convo traffic patterns (avg tokens/turn, typical context length) — one-week trace or a small synthetic trace.
3) Confirm whether EU traffic must remain in-customer VPC (yes/no).
4) Any constrained latency SLA or tolerance for canary periods.

What we recommend for initial evals (Redwood Recommendations)
- Baseline candidate: redwood-7b-l10n (FP16) — strong balance for idiomatic handling in EU languages.
- Cost-efficient variant: redwood-3b-quant (4-bit) — good for prototypes; watch for occasional token-level regressions on idioms.
- High-recall for QA: l10n-super-13b (FP16) — when precision+style are both critical.

Attachments included: prompt_sets_v1.zip (prompt templates + seed examples), locale_benchmarks_20261121.csv (initial smoke-run results on our internal small eval).

Next steps / asks (owner)
- Anna: share sample test sets + confirm residency requirement (by 2026-11-24).
- Marissa (solutions): run 3 quick smoke evals across the three EU locales using the attachments (deliverable: short report, by 2026-11-28).
- Neha (research): prepare quantization/latency profiles for redwood-3b-quant and redwood-7b-l10n (by 2026-11-29).
- Aditya: schedule a 60-minute model-review workshop (propose Fri 2026-11-26 or Mon 2026-11-29).

Anything you want added to that checklist? Happy to tighten the evaluation rubric if you have specific user-critical prompts.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0121

Hi Aditya / Marissa —

Thanks for the clear notes. A couple quick Qs: 
1) For EU data residency — we need EU-hosted inference (no egress of EU PII) and would prefer a private deployment if Redwood supports it. Can you confirm options and an engagement path?
2) On hallucination: do you have any quantifiable metrics or observed failure modes on 'product-answer' style prompts (our concern is false product info returned to end users)?
3) Is there a recommended confidence score or fallback policy we should implement client-side while you run canaries?

I'll try to send a 300-example dev set (mixed idioms + typical support questions) by Tue 24th. For the traffic pattern, I'll pull a 48h sample with tokens/turns.

Also curious on costs — can you ballpark cost-per-1000-tokens for redwood-7b-l10n vs redwood-3b-quant in a dedicated/reserved capacity scenario?

Best,
Anna
Head of Product Operations
LinguaWorks
anna.schubert@linguaworks.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Anna Schubert <anna.schubert@linguaworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T12:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilang qualification checklist + prompt sets (EU & APAC)

Anna —

Great questions, brief answers + links and samples below.

1) EU residency / private deployment
- Yes — Redwood Private (VPC) supports EU-only inference with customer-controlled egress. We can do a short scoping engagement (2–4 days) to finalize network + KMS. I'll loop in our solutions architect if you want to fast-track.

2) Hallucination / failure modes
- Short answer: hallucinations are more common on low-resource idiomatic prompts and when the model is aggressively compressed. In our internal smoke-run (attached CSV) we saw redwood-3b-quant had a ~6% higher hallucination proxy (measured via a keyword-based hallucination detector on the dev set) vs redwood-7b-l10n. That corresponds to ~5–8 additional manual corrections per 1k responses in the worst locales.
- Longer answer / suggested tests: run a 'product-fact' prompt set (we included a small seed in prompt_sets_v1.zip: product_fact_check_de.md). We'll help you run a canary that flags low-confidence answers for human review.

3) Confidence / fallback
- We recommend a 2-tier approach: soft-confidence threshold that triggers re-prompting (+system prompt tightness) and a hard threshold to route to a deterministic fallback (template response or support handoff). Neha — attaching a sample scoring config (we'll share full scoring config in the workshop).

4) Costs (high level) — dedicated capacity, estimate per 1k tokens (approx):
- redwood-3b-quant: $0.18 per 1k tokens (reserved pricing depends on commit)
- redwood-7b-l10n: $0.36 per 1k tokens
- l10n-super-13b (FP16): $0.90 per 1k tokens
(we'll give a line-item once we know throughput & retention patterns)

Quick recommendation for immediate qualification:
- Run 3 smoke evals (we'll provide eval harness): redwood-3b-quant, redwood-7b-l10n, l10n-super-13b. Focus first on DE/FR/ES. If redwood-3b-quant shows idiom regressions, plan a canary at 10% traffic with a short-stay fallback to 7b.

Links / attachments
- Benchmark run: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/runs/9812-localization (contains the smoke-run that generated locale_benchmarks_20261121.csv)
- Prompt examples (excerpt):
  > de_product_fact_check: 
  > System: You are a factual assistant for LinguaWorks product pages. Confirm whether the statement is true or false and cite the field.
  > User: "Unser Produkt unterstützt CSV-Export bis zu 10.000 Zeilen."
  > Assistant: (should answer True/False with a short rationale)

Next steps: I'll schedule a 60-min workshop slot on Mon 2026-11-29 10:00–11:00 PST unless you prefer Fri. I'll also put together the scoring config and a short canary playbook.

Thanks — will wait for your dev set.

-Aditya

--
